chunks.arabic_text: عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ أَبِي حَمَّادَ، كُوفِيٌّ، سَكَنَ قُمٌ، وَرَوَى عَنْهُ الْقُمِّيُونَ، يُكْنَى أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ. ضَعِيفٌ جِدًّا، لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَيْهِ، فِي مَذْهَبِهِ غُلُوٌّ.

translations.en: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad, Kufan. He settled in Qum, and the people of Qum narrated from him. He is known by the kunya Abu Muhammad. Very weak, not relied upon, in his madhhab there is ghulw (exaggeration).

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Du‘afā’* highlights Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ḥammād, a Kufan narrator who migrated to Qum and became a focal point for local scholars. His classification as 'very weak' (ḥadathan) and his tendency toward *ghulw* (exaggeration in Imamology) reflect the critical scrutiny applied to narrators during the formative period of Shia hadith sciences, particularly as the center of narration shifted from Kufa to Qum.
en.seo_question: Who is Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?
